title: The Moon and Sun Pull the Sea Up and Down
description: Why the ocean rises and falls twice a day, explained with NOAA and Britannica.
narration: Why does the sea rise and fall twice a day? Tides are caused by the pull of the Moon and the Sun. The Sun's effect is similar to the Moon's and adds to it. When the Sun, Moon and Earth line up, tides get higher and lower than usual. Tides are very long-period waves moving through the ocean. Most places have about two high tides and two low tides every day. The gap in height between high and low tide is called the tidal range.
